title: Can the Lemonade Stand Always Give Change?

concept.title: When there are two ways to give change, use the one that keeps the more useful bills
body: A lemonade costs 5. Customers stand in a queue and each pays with **one bill** of 5, 10 or 20, and you must give the right change at once from the bills you have received so far (you start with no money). Can you serve all the customers in order? For `5 5 5 10 20` yes; for `5 5 10 10 20` no: after the first four customers you hold two 10-bills and no 5-bill, so the change of 15 for the last customer cannot be given.

Count the bills you hold: `fives` and `tens` (twenties are never given as change, so they need no count). A 5-bill needs no change. A 10-bill needs the change 5: one five. A 20-bill needs the change 15, and there are two ways: **one 10 and one 5**, or **three 5s**. The greedy rule: **prefer the 10 and the 5**. Why? A 10-bill is useful only for giving change to a 20, while 5-bills are useful for everybody, so keep the 5s. If you cannot make the change, the answer is no.

body.code:
fives = tens = 0
ok = True
for bill in bills:
    if bill == 5:
        fives += 1
    elif bill == 10:
        if fives == 0: ok = False; break
        fives -= 1; tens += 1
    else:                                   # 20: change 15
        if tens > 0 and fives > 0: tens -= 1; fives -= 1
        elif fives >= 3: fives -= 3
        else: ok = False; break
print("yes" if ok else "no")

body: The choice "10 + 5 before 5 + 5 + 5" is the greedy decision, and it is safe by the same exchange argument: any plan that uses three 5s while a 10 is available can use the 10 instead and keep two 5s more. The simulation takes O(n) time and O(1) memory.

statement: A lemonade costs 5. `n` customers come in order; each pays with one bill of 5, 10 or 20 and must get the right change immediately, using only the bills received from the earlier customers (there is no money at the start). Print `yes` if every customer can be served, otherwise `no`.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of customers.
The second line has `n` numbers, each 5, 10 or 20: the bill that each customer pays with, in the order of the queue.

examples.note: Change 5 for the 10, change 10 + 5 for the 20: yes.
The second 10 uses the last 5; for the 20 there is only one 10 and no 5: no.

hints: A 20 needs 15 in change: use a 10 and a 5 if possible, otherwise three 5s.
Stop with no as soon as the change cannot be given.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
bills = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: The number of 5-bills and 10-bills held is tracked. A 5 needs no change, a 10 needs a 5, and a 20 is changed with a 10 and a 5 when possible (the greedy choice, since 5s are more useful) and with three 5s otherwise; if the change cannot be given the answer is no.
